---
title: "Account backup and restore through GitHub"
date: 2026-11-23
lang: en
---

The problem: every device of a Jami account is lost, or the OS is reinstalled. Today the
account is then gone: Jami can only bring it back by linking from a device that still has
it. Joma users on Omarchy are logged into GitHub and often run an agent, so GitHub can
hold an encrypted backup, and Joma (or the agent) can restore from it on a fresh machine.
It goes with the identity check (`2026-11-18-github-identity.qmd`): the restored account
has the same Jami ID, so contacts and the GitHub badge stay valid.

Checked in `upstream/jami-daemon`:

- `exportToFile(account, path, scheme, password)` writes the account archive: account
  key, contacts, username, device list, config. `password` is the account's own Jami
  password (it reads and re-saves the archive with it, `archive_account_manager.cpp:1523`),
  not a new passphrase. Joma creates accounts without one, so the exported file is
  **not encrypted**. Joma must encrypt it itself.
- Import is `addAccount` with `Account.archivePath` (and the archive's password, empty
  here). The stock Jami app can import the same decrypted file.
- Conversation history is not in the archive: it lives in the conversations' git
  repositories and comes back from contacts (and other devices) when they are online.

Sketch: Joma exports the archive, encrypts it with a passphrase (`age` with scrypt, or
the same in Rust), and pushes it to a private repo `joma-backup`, one file per account
plus an `index.json` (names, Jami IDs, dates; no secrets). Restoring decrypts the file
and calls `addAccount`. This machine becomes a new device of the account; the devices
tab then offers to revoke the lost ones.

# 1. Where the backup lives

A private repo `joma-backup` (getting it needs your GitHub login, opening it needs the
passphrase), or a secret gist (unlisted, but anyone with its URL can download it, so the
passphrase is the only lock). Proposal: the private repo. Joma refuses to write into a
repo that is public.

- [ ] A:

# 2. How Joma talks to GitHub

An OAuth App can only ask for `repo`, which reaches every private repo you have. A GitHub
App can be limited to the one `joma-backup` repo (contents read and write) and also hold
the gists permission for the identity check. Proposal: one GitHub App "Joma", registered
by you, with the device flow; when `gh` is logged in, Joma can use it instead and skip
its own login.

- [ ] A:

# 3. The passphrase

Anyone who gets the file can guess passphrases offline. Proposal: Joma suggests a
generated one (6 random words), accepts your own only if it is long enough, and says
plainly that a lost passphrase makes the backup useless (keep it in your password
manager). One passphrase for all accounts, or one each?

- [ ] A:

# 4. The agent

Proposal: the agent may fetch files and run `joma backup` / `joma restore <file>`, but
the passphrase is always typed into Joma's own window, never passed on the command line
or through the agent (transcripts and logs keep it). Is there more the agent should do,
for example check that the backup is recent, or run it on a schedule?

- [ ] A:

# 5. Keeping the backup current

The archive changes when you add contacts or devices. Options: a "back up now" button
and a reminder when the backup is older than the last contact change; or automatic
backups, which keep a token on the machine (acceptable with a one-repo GitHub App).
Proposal: automatic, with the token in the system keyring, and off until you turn it on.

- [ ] A:

# 6. Conversation history

Not in the archive. It comes back from contacts when they are online, and only for the
conversations they still have. Backing up the conversations too is possible (much
bigger, holds message contents and received files). Proposal: not in the first version;
accounts only.

- [ ] A:

# 7. Which accounts

Proposal: you choose per account; agent accounts are listed too, off by default.

- [ ] A:

# 8. Where restore starts

Proposal: on the first-start screen ("restore from GitHub" next to create and link),
in the accounts tab ("add → restore from GitHub"), and `joma restore` on the command
line.

- [ ] A:

# 9. Logging in on a new machine while the old one still works

That is Jami's normal linking. An agent on the old machine could help (`joma link
<code>`), but a file on GitHub should not approve a link by itself: write access to the
repo would then be enough to add a device to your account. Proposal: keep linking as it
is; the backup is for when every device is gone.

- [ ] A:
